task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: derived play-type possession records from play-by-play
label data quality and points attribution
methodological_questions: Does opponent next-possession PPP after play X exceed a magnitude large enough to drive AVOID labels?
Are own-sequence lagged PPP effects of play X material for labeling?
Is the AVOID label computed from the same possession outcome (points) that the test uses as its response, creating outcome-derived label leakage?
What sample size and exposure per play type and lag are needed for adequate power?
How reliable are play-type labels and points attribution across 2022-23 to 2025-26?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned no records, so no earlier study by this project is available in this setting to establish any finding about opponent next-possession PPP, AVOID labels, or own-sequence lags.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether any prior analysis of play X, opponent PPP, or AVOID labeling has been run.
Whether earlier label-reliability or leakage checks exist for the derived possession records.
Any effect size, direction, or failure mode for the question as posed.
own_inferences: The question as posed is a conditional, descriptive effect question that can be tested with the stated per-game play-by-play and derived possession data if the AVOID label and possession linkage are defined precisely.

The AVOID label, as described, appears to depend on the next-possession points that the question then treats as the outcome. Unless the label is defined from data excluded from the test window, the test would be circular.
Per-play-type and per-lag cells may be sparse, so the test should pool across seasons and use a pre-specified set of play types and lags.
uncertainties: The exact definition of the AVOID label and its threshold is not given in the task statement.
The definition of 'play X' (initiator, play type, sub-type) and of possession boundaries in [source] database is not given.
Whether the derived records attribute points to the correct possession (for example, and-ones, offensive rebounds, and free throws) has not been verified.
The 2025-26 playoffs were only complete from 2026-06-21, so they should be excluded from a 2026-06-19 data freeze.
Drift in play-type tagging and pace across seasons is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: No records were returned, so the decision rests on the task statement and the data description alone. The retrieval neither supports nor rejects the question, and it does not reveal any previously identified failure.

blocking_constraints.text: If AVOID is derived from next-possession points, the response and label are the same quantity. The test must define the label from a source that is independent of the response, or the association is tautological.
Individual play types and lags may have few possessions per team-season, so cell-level PPP estimates may be too noisy to support AVOID thresholds without pooling.
Play-type tags and points attribution from play-by-play may be inconsistent, which limits the reliability of both the exposure and the outcome.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. No prior-work identifiers are relied on.

risks.text: AVOID labels built from next-possession points make the PPP effect partly definitional. Label construction must be separated from the outcome used in the test.
Using possession outcomes that occur after the labeled play, or data from the full season to define labels for earlier plays, would leak future information into the test.
Sparse play-type and lag cells can produce unstable PPP estimates and spurious large effects.
The effect of a single play type on next-possession PPP is likely small relative to possession-level noise, so power may be inadequate without pooling.
Testing many play types and lags across opponents invites false positives unless the family of tests is fixed in advance.
Lineup, opponent quality, pace, score state, and shot quality can confound the association between play X and next-possession PPP.
Points attribution and play-type tags in the derived graph records may contain errors that bias PPP and label assignment.
Mislabeled plays or misassigned possession boundaries would misclassify AVOID status.
Graph-database derivation of possession records may contain join or ordering errors that create artificial lag effects.
Rule changes, tagging changes, and pace shifts across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may change the PPP distribution by season.
Overall next-possession PPP is the baseline; small shifts relative to it may not be large enough to drive AVOID decisions, so the threshold must be justified.
Without placebo lags or placebo plays, an association may reflect generic possession-sequence structure rather than play X.

design.estimand: Difference in opponent next-possession PPP after play X versus matched non-X possessions, by lag, and whether that difference exceeds a pre-specified AVOID threshold; plus the same for own-sequence lags.
design.unit: Possession (the play X event and the following opponent possession), nested within game and team-season.
design.sample: Regular-season games from 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25, plus 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs under the 2026-06-19 freeze. Playoffs from 2022-23 to 2024-25 can be used as a secondary sample.
design.power: Compute power before analysis using the pooled possession count for each pre-specified play type. Pool across seasons; drop cells below a pre-specified minimum (for example, 500 possessions), and report them as untestable rather than estimating them.
design.controls: Score margin and game state, period and clock, home/away, opponent identity and team-season fixed effects, lineup or starter indicators where available, and shot distance and result for the preceding play. Use defensive matchup minutes as a covariate. Define the AVOID label from a source independent of the response (for example, a pre-specified rule fixed before the outcome window) and exclude the outcome possession from label construction.
design.falsification: Placebo lags (lag -1 and lags before play X), placebo plays with no expected effect, and a split-sample check in which labels are derived from one season and the PPP effect is estimated in another. Also audit possession-boundary and points attribution on a random sample of games against the raw play-by-play.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register the set of play types and lags. Control the family-wise or false-discovery rate across them (for example, Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg), and report unadjusted and adjusted estimates.
design.decision_rule: Declare an AVOID-level effect only if the pre-specified threshold is exceeded with a confidence interval that excludes the threshold after multiplicity correction, the effect replicates in a held-out season, and placebo lags and plays show no comparable effect. Otherwise report inconclusive or artifact.
design.data_version: Data frozen as of 2026-06-19: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs excluded because they were incomplete before 2026-06-21. Record [source]-database derivation version and the play-by-play extraction date.
